answer.question: What do student success stories at Icanio Tech School show?
answer.answer: They show students from colleges across Tamil Nadu completing mentored internships in tracks such as DevOps, UI/UX, AI/ML, Java and Spring Boot, data analytics and digital marketing. Durations range from one week to three months. More than 1,000 students have been placed, 90% within five months, and Jeyaram R went on to join Icanio Technologies as an SDE.

sections.heading: From Icanio Tech School to Icanio Technologies
sections.intro: One of our proudest student success stories is also the most direct: a student who learned with us and now builds with us.
paragraphs: Jeyaram R was a student of Icanio Tech School. He learned through structured, hands-on programs led by practising Icanio engineers. He put in steady effort, built real skills and made the most of the opportunities in front of him.

Today, Jeyaram has begun his professional journey as a Software Development Engineer at Icanio Technologies. He moved from the classroom side of the company to the delivery side. His path shows how focused learning, consistent practice and the right exposure can turn into a real career.

We share his story because it shows what our referral route means in practice. Top performers are referred to the Icanio talent team. When a student proves themselves on real project work, the next step can be a role in the same company.
bullets: Learned at Icanio Tech School with practising engineers
Built skills on hands-on, project-based work
Joined Icanio Technologies as a Software Development Engineer

sections.heading: What our interns say in their own words
sections.intro: Written student success stories from interns in tracks like Python, Java and Digital Twin. More reviews appear on each internship page.

items.name: Kevin Abishek
items.quote: I'm Kevin Abishek, a first-year B.E. Computer Science student who completed a one-week Python internship at Icanio Technologies, working on mentor-assigned tasks that sharpened my programming, problem-solving, and debugging skills. The key lesson I learned was to keep going instead of giving up when errors appeared, to analyse the problem, debug carefully, and find the right solution, while also writing clean code and asking for guidance when needed.

items.name: Jerusha Glory Angelin
items.quote: I'm Jerusha Glory Angelin, a final-year Computer Science and Engineering student, and I interned in the Digital Twin domain at Icanio Technologies, gaining hands-on experience developing 3D visualisations using NVIDIA Isaac Sim Omniverse. The internship taught me the importance of teamwork and the growing role of AI across every field, and working in Isaac Sim Omniverse was the biggest technical challenge I tackled.

items.name: Jebinskaran
items.quote: I'm currently learning Java fundamentals, variables, loops, arrays, classes, and basic object-oriented programming, and during my internship I assisted with Java-based tasks, writing simple programs, debugging basic code, and understanding how Java is applied in real-world applications, while also getting exposure to IDEs like Eclipse and IntelliJ and best practices for clean, readable code.

items.name: Sri Varshini
items.quote: I'm Sri Varshini M, pursuing my Bachelor's in Computer Science and Engineering, and I focused during my internship on Python programming, Data Structures and Algorithms, Git, and GitHub, actively taking part in training sessions, coding exercises, and hands-on activities. The most valuable lesson was the importance of a strong foundation in the basics, since deeply understanding fundamentals makes it far easier to solve problems and apply knowledge in real-world situations.

items.name: Harsith
items.quote: I'm Harsith NV, a Computer Science student at Shiv Nadar University with a strong foundation in systems architecture and competitive programming, and my internship focused on intensive training, absorbing enterprise development standards and industry best practices to build a rigorous technical foundation. The most valuable lesson was learning to bridge academic concepts with enterprise execution, realising that effective code isn't just about functionality but about creating scalable, maintainable solutions that hold up under rigorous review.

items.name: Thanga Dharshini
items.college: Kamaraj College of Engineering and Technology
items.quote: I'm Thanga Dharshini R, and after first learning Android development with Kotlin, I worked during my internship as a backend developer on a project called Pulse, gaining real-world experience with Python and the Django framework by developing and managing backend functionality. The most valuable lesson was learning how to apply technical knowledge to real projects, manage tasks effectively, and work as part of a team to solve problems.

items.name: Sugi Brighty
items.quote: I'm Sugi Brighty, a BCA student, and during this internship I learned Java and worked on practical tasks and projects to build my technical skills. The most valuable lesson was learning how to apply classroom knowledge to real-world tasks, along with the importance of teamwork, communication, and continuous learning. Improving my communication skills alongside grasping new concepts was the main challenge, which I worked through with regular practice and guidance from my mentors.

items.name: Lakshmi
items.college: Dr. Sivanthi Aditanar College of Engineering
items.quote: Hello, I'm Lakshmi from Tirunelveli, pursuing my final year B.Tech in Information Technology at Dr. Sivanthi Aditanar College of Engineering, and during my internship I learned the basics of Java and Spring Boot, Core Java, OOP concepts, Collections, Exception Handling, REST APIs, and foundational Spring Boot concepts. The most valuable lesson was adapting to a new environment and people, building a wider professional network, understanding how developers work on real projects, and recognising that while AI tools are useful for reference and syntax, real skill comes from building projects with your own ability.

sections.heading: What makes these student success stories possible
sections.intro: None of these results came from a certificate alone. They came from how the work is set up.
paragraphs: Every intern works with a 1:1 mentor who is a practising Icanio engineer or specialist. The mentor reviews code, designs or reports each week to internal Icanio standards. Feedback is specific, so students know exactly what to fix.

Interns work on briefs drawn from real Icanio client scenarios. They use Git, join stand-ups and move in sprints. By the end, they have a project they can explain in detail: the problem, the trade-offs and what they would change next time.

Our team also prepares students for the step after the internship. We run resume building, mock interviews and LinkedIn guidance. Portfolio reviews are done by Icanio hiring managers. Top performers are referred to the Icanio talent team, which is how several student success stories continue into jobs.
bullets: 1:1 mentorship from an engineer on live projects
Weekly reviews to internal Icanio standards
Projects based on real client scenarios
Resume, mock interview and LinkedIn support

sections.heading: Habits we see in our student success stories
sections.intro: When our team looks back at student success stories, the same habits appear again and again. None of them need prior experience. All of them can be learned.
items: They pick a track that matches a real interest, not only a trend
They show up to every check-in, even when progress is slow
They treat review comments as a to-do list, not as criticism
They ask questions early instead of staying stuck for days
They finish the project fully and document what they built
They practise explaining their work before the final demo

sections.heading: How to use these stories to choose your internship
paragraphs: Start with your degree and your interest. The stories above include computer science and IT students, an MCA student and a data science student. Each one picked a track that built on what they already knew. A CSE student with a feel for design chose UI/UX. An IT student curious about infrastructure chose DevOps.

Next, think about time. If you have a short break between semesters, a one-week or 15-day internship gives you a focused start. If you have a longer window, a one-month to three-month internship lets you ship a bigger project and go deeper with your mentor.

Finally, talk to our team. A counsellor can look at your year of study, your skills and your goals, then suggest a track and duration. We recommend deciding with a clear goal in mind, such as a first job, a portfolio project or a switch into a new field.

sections.heading: Student success stories from partner colleges
paragraphs: Many of our student success stories begin with a college partnership. Through an MoU, partner colleges get priority access to workshops, value added courses and free or sponsored internships for their students. Placement officers receive progress updates, so they can track each student's journey.

For a placement cell, student success stories like these are useful evidence. They show which tracks students chose, how long they trained and what they built. Our team can share a summary for your college after each batch, which helps you plan the next semester.

faqs.q: Are these student success stories real?
faqs.a: Yes. Every completion on this page is a verified internship at Icanio Tech School, listed with the student's track, duration, degree and college. The video testimonials are recorded by the interns themselves. We only publish stories with the student's consent.

faqs.q: Did Jeyaram R really join Icanio Technologies?
faqs.a: Yes. Jeyaram R was a student of Icanio Tech School and began his professional journey as a Software Development Engineer at Icanio Technologies. His story shows how our referral route works: top performers are referred to the Icanio talent team for roles.

faqs.q: How many students have been placed after training?
faqs.a: More than 2,000 students have trained with Icanio Tech School and more than 1,000 have been placed. Around 90% of placed students found roles within five months of completing their program. Placement depends on your effort, project quality and interview preparation.

faqs.q: Can a short internship lead to student success stories?
faqs.a: A short internship of one week or 15 days is a good first step. It gives you a taste of the track and a certificate. For a project strong enough to discuss in interviews, we recommend one to three months, as many of these student success stories show.

faqs.q: Do non-engineering students succeed in these programs?
faqs.a: Yes. Our tracks include data analytics, digital marketing, HR, finance and sales. Two of the recent completions on this page are three-month digital marketing internships, and a data analytics intern came from a B.Sc. Data Science and Statistics program.

faqs.q: Which colleges do these interns come from?
faqs.a: They come from colleges across Tamil Nadu, including Francis Xavier Engineering College, Karpagam College of Engineering, Karunya Institute of Technology and Science, Ramco Institute of Technology, Kongu Engineering College and Government College of Engineering, Tirunelveli.

faqs.q: Will I get a certificate after my internship?
faqs.a: Yes. Every intern who completes a program receives an Icanio Tech School certificate that states the track and duration. You also leave with portfolio work reviewed by Icanio engineers, which is often what employers ask about first.

faqs.q: How can I share my own story after completing?
faqs.a: Tell your mentor or our team when you finish. With your consent, we can feature your completion or record a short video testimonial. It helps future students choose a track, and it adds a public, verifiable proof point to your profile.

faqs.q: Why do student success stories matter when choosing an internship?
faqs.a: Student success stories show you what real interns achieved, not just what a brochure promises. Look for verified names, tracks, durations and colleges. Check whether interns shipped real projects and whether anyone was hired. That tells you more about a program than a list of topics.

takeaways: These student success stories are verified completions from colleges across Tamil Nadu.
Tracks include DevOps, UI/UX, AI/ML, Java and Spring Boot, data analytics, Digital Twin and digital marketing.
More than 1,000 students have been placed, and 90% were placed within five months.
Jeyaram R went from Icanio Tech School to a Software Development Engineer role at Icanio Technologies.
Mentorship, real client briefs and interview preparation are what make these student success stories possible.
conclusion: Behind every one of these student success stories is the same formula: a real project, a mentor who reviews your work every week and a clear path to the next step.
Your story can start this month. Choose a track, talk to our team and join a batch that fits your college schedule. We look forward to adding your name to our student success stories.
